points.reason: The process computes and holds the decoded instruction from instr_i, releases it through instr_o, and can make the output unusable through illegal, but it has no privileged, override or bypass behavior.
instr_o exposes the decoded instruction, while illegal can alter instr_o(1) and clear part of the instruction to block execution; this is not a separate privileged or bypass behavior.

The process computes illegal from instruction-field checks, so tampering can change the legality decision, and the resulting value can clear instr_o(1) and block execution; the decision is not exposed and has no special override behavior.

The output assignment uses illegal to clear instr_o(1), so this release point can prevent functional instruction availability, but it neither exposes nor changes the legality decision itself and has no special behavior.
